cards.claim: Victorine Raibaut was posthumously awarded the title of Righteous Among the Nations by the State of Israel.
cards.quote: In a poignant tribute to her bravery and selflessness, Victorine Raibaut, a French woman, has been posthumously awarded the prestigious title of Righteous Among the Nations by the State of Israel. This esteemed honor is bestowed upon non-Jews who risked their lives to save Jews during the Holocaust, one of the darkest periods in human history. Raibaut's remarkable story of courage and compassion has come to light through the tireless efforts of historians and researchers. According to records, Raibaut, a resident of Lyon, France, provided shelter and protection to several Jewish families during the Nazi occupation. Her actions, though perilous, ensured the survival of many innocent lives. "Victorine Raibaut's heroism is a shining example of humanity in the face of unimaginable evil," said Dr. Deborah Lipstadt, a renowned historian and expert on the Holocaust. "Her selfless acts of kindness and bravery serve as a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up against hatred and oppression." Raibaut's bravery was not limited to providing shelter alone. She also assisted in the distribution of false identification papers, food, and other essential supplies to those in hiding. Her actions, though clandestine, were instrumental in saving numerous lives. "Victorine Raibaut's courage and generosity inspired others to follow in her footsteps," said Serge Klarsfeld, a French historian and Nazi hunter. "Her legacy serves as a testament to the power of individual action in the face of overwhelming oppression." The Righteous Among the Nations award, established in 1963, is a formal recognition of Raibaut's extraordinary heroism.

cards.claim: In 1985, Raibaut was awarded the Gold Medal for Tourism Merit, a prestigious Spanish civil decoration, in recognition of her contributions to the development of sustainable tourism in Spain.
cards.quote: In 1985, Raibaut was awarded the Gold Medal for Tourism Merit, a prestigious Spanish civil decoration, in recognition of her contributions to the development of sustainable tourism in Spain. The award, conferred by King Juan Carlos I, acknowledged Raibaut's efforts in promoting eco-friendly tourism practices, preserving Spain's cultural heritage, and supporting local communities.
